text: The project manager moved cost review ahead of the prototype presentation because the current concept exceeded the production allowance and required redesign.
The team iteratively compared cost-saving changes to controls, power, casing, colour and speech recognition rather than accepting every early suggestion.
They retained the LCD because the design depended on its menus and removed speech recognition to save cost, despite reported stronger survey interest in speech.
The revised design used a single integrated scroll-wheel/pushbutton with no separate buttons, a hand dynamo, and a single-curved plastic case; the project manager reported it within budget.
Marketing led an internal team rating of the revised design, using a seven-point scale and criteria derived from user requirements, market trends and company strategy.

The team calculated 28/9, approximately 3.11, with lower scores considered better. The industrial designer questioned the item polarity; marketing explained the intended positive wording and the industrial designer accepted that explanation, while shortcomings remained.
The industrial and user interface designers redrew the revised remote while the project manager worked on the final report with help from the marketing expert.
The project manager led a short evaluation of the team interaction, project steps, creativity and tools.
Participants felt their coordination and shared understanding improved over successive meetings, especially from the first to the second.
They felt there had been room for creativity, but late financial constraints limited the design.
Participants preferred the digital pen's operation to the SMARTboard, while finding PowerPoint useful for presentation but awkward for quick drawing and learning.
The project manager will complete the final report covering the team's decisions and financial redesign, with the marketing expert assisting.
deadline: ten minutes after the final meeting ends

text: Use a single-curved case, replacing the double-curved concept.
Drop speech recognition while retaining the LCD and its menu-based concept.
Replace the rubber casing with plastic, while retaining special colour for the design.
Use one integrated scroll-wheel/pushbutton and no separate buttons, with functions accessed through the LCD; detailed click/hold/menu behavior was not fully settled.
Replace kinetic power with a hand dynamo after considering a battery and other cost reductions.
The design cost about EUR 25 at the start of this meeting against a EUR 12.50 production allowance. The team reduced features and the project manager later reported it within budget.

text: The group initially disagreed about which features and controls to cut; it settled on retaining the LCD, removing speech, simplifying controls and using cheaper casing/power choices.

Cost information arrived after concept/prototype work, forcing substantial rework. Participants said the financial review should have occurred before drawing; the process problem had no agreed preventive fix.

The industrial designer questioned whether mixed positive/negative wording invalidated the mean score. Marketing explained the intended positive criteria and the industrial designer accepted that explanation within the meeting.
The industrial designer and user interface designer will redraw the remote to match the reduced-cost, one-control design; the recorded drawing was revised during the meeting.

The marketing expert will present the prepared evaluation procedure and lead the team's assessment of the revised design; the procedure, internal ratings and mean calculation were completed during this meeting.
